title: Centered noise difference norm bound
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian probability measure $\gamma^n$. The $L^1(\gamma^n)$ norm of the difference between the Gaussian noise of $f$ with parameter $\rho$ and the Gaussian mean $\int f\,d\gamma^n$ is at most the $L^1(\gamma^n\times\gamma^n)$ norm of $(x,y)\mapsto f(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,y)-f(y)$, with the operations on vectors taken coordinatewise.
hypotheses_covered: $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure
